=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Block-Lists.md === # FEATURE: Block Lists | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20260815 V1 | | Description | Parse nested bullet and ordered lists with CommonMark tightness and lazy continuation. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md, FEATURE-Block-References.md | | Provides | list nodes, list item nodes, tight and loose list state | | Consumes | block quote nodes, leaf blocks, document-wide link reference definition map | ## Questions - None. ## Workflow List parsing consumes normalized input after block quotes and reference definitions are available. Recognize bullet and ordered markers, determine item content indentation, recursively parse contained blocks, and group adjacent items only when their marker types match. Track list tightness from blank lines between items and between directly contained blocks. Preserve ordered-list start numbers, empty items, nested lists, lazy paragraph continuation, and delimiter changes. Render paragraph wrappers according to the computed tight or loose state. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC block-lists-conformance === Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark examples for list items and lists owned by this story. Suite: scoped import subprocess result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", r"^(List items|Lists)$", ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC block-lists-conformance === === AC block-lists-selector === Intent: The list conformance selector executes the owned specification sections successfully. Suite: scoped import subprocess sections = r"^(List items|Lists)$" result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", sections, ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC block-lists-selector === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from this story. - Preserve CommonMark block-before-inline parsing. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Inline-Escapes.md === # FEATURE: Inline Escapes | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20260815 V1 | | Description | Parse backslash escapes and named or numeric character references in inline content. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Block-Lists.md | | Provides | escaped punctuation, named entity references, numeric character references | | Consumes | block tree, document-wide link reference definition map | ## Questions - None. ## Workflow Parse inline text after block structure has been established. Remove backslashes only when they precede ASCII punctuation, preserve backslashes before other characters, and decode valid HTML5 named entities plus decimal and hexadecimal numeric references. Apply reference parsing outside code spans, fenced code, indented code, autolinks, and raw HTML. Replace U+0000 and invalid numeric code points with U+FFFD, while leaving invalid or unterminated references as literal text. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC inline-escapes-conformance === Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark examples for backslash escapes and entity or numeric character references owned by this story. Suite: scoped import subprocess result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", r"^(Backslash escapes|Entity and numeric character references)$", ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-escapes-conformance === === AC inline-escapes-selector === Intent: The escape and character-reference conformance selector executes successfully. Suite: scoped import subprocess sections = r"^(Backslash escapes|Entity and numeric character references)$" result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", sections, ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-escapes-selector === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not decode entities or escapes inside code spans or code blocks. - Do not treat entity references as block-structure markers. - Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from this story. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Inline-Code-Breaks.md === # FEATURE: Inline Code Breaks | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20260815 V1 | | Description | Parse code spans and hard or soft line breaks according to CommonMark. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Inline-Escapes.md | | Provides | code spans, hard line breaks, soft line breaks | | Consumes | escaped inline content, block tree | ## Questions - None. ## Workflow Recognize backtick strings and pair only delimiters of equal length. Normalize line endings inside code spans to spaces, remove one surrounding space when both ends contain spaces and the content is not all spaces, and preserve all other code content literally. For ordinary inline text, convert a line ending preceded by two or more spaces or a backslash into `
` behavior when it is not at block end. Preserve soft line breaks as line endings, remove indentation at the beginning of the continuation line, and leave code spans and HTML tags unaffected. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC inline-code-breaks-conformance === Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark examples for code spans and hard or soft line breaks owned by this story. Suite: scoped import subprocess result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", r"^(Code spans|Hard line breaks|Soft line breaks)$", ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-code-breaks-conformance === === AC inline-code-breaks-selector === Intent: The code-span and line-break conformance selector executes successfully. Suite: scoped import subprocess sections = r"^(Code spans|Hard line breaks|Soft line breaks)$" result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", sections, ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-code-breaks-selector === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not apply escapes or entity references inside code spans. - Do not emit hard breaks at the end of a block. - Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from this story. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Inline-Emphasis.md === # FEATURE: Inline Emphasis | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20260815 V1 | | Description | Parse emphasis and strong emphasis with the CommonMark delimiter-run algorithm. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Inline-Code-Breaks.md | | Provides | emphasis and strong-emphasis inline nodes | | Consumes | code spans, escaped inline content, block tree | ## Questions - None. ## Workflow Build delimiter runs for asterisks and underscores while parsing inline content. Compute left- and right-flanking behavior using Unicode whitespace and punctuation, apply intraword restrictions for underscores, and resolve matching delimiters with the CommonMark delimiter-stack algorithm. Support single and double emphasis, nested emphasis, rule-of-three behavior, precedence against code spans and other inline constructs, and unmatched delimiter runs. Preserve literal delimiters when no valid pairing exists. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC inline-emphasis-conformance === Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark examples for emphasis and strong emphasis owned by this story. Suite: scoped import subprocess result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", r"^Emphasis and strong emphasis$", ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-emphasis-conformance === === AC inline-emphasis-selector === Intent: The emphasis conformance selector executes the complete owned specification section successfully. Suite: scoped import subprocess section = r"^Emphasis and strong emphasis$" result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", section, ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-emphasis-selector === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Apply delimiter matching only after code spans, links, images, and raw HTML precedence is respected. - Do not allow intraword underscore emphasis. - Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from this story. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Inline-Links.md === # FEATURE: Inline Links | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20260815 V1 | | Description | Parse inline, reference, collapsed, and shortcut links together with images. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Inline-Emphasis.md, FEATURE-Block-References.md | | Provides | links and images with destinations, titles, references, and alt text | | Consumes | emphasis inline nodes, code spans, document-wide link reference definition map | ## Questions - None. ## Workflow Recognize bracketed link text and image descriptions before resolving inline, full-reference, collapsed-reference, and shortcut forms. Parse balanced destinations, angle-bracket destinations, optional titles, escapes, entities, and permitted line endings. Resolve labels using the document-wide first-definition map. Prevent nested links while allowing nested images, and construct image alt text from the plain textual content of the description. Preserve literal brackets and source text when a candidate does not satisfy the link grammar. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC inline-links-conformance === Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark examples for links and images owned by this story. Suite: scoped import subprocess result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", r"^(Links|Images)$", ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-links-conformance === === AC inline-links-selector === Intent: The link and image conformance selector executes the complete owned specification sections successfully. Suite: scoped import subprocess sections = r"^(Links|Images)$" result = subprocess.run( [ "python3", "sources/spec_tests.py", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--program", "./commonmark", "--pattern", sections, ], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC inline-links-selector === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not resolve references before block parsing has collected document-wide definitions. - Do not permit links nested inside links. - Preserve image descriptions as plain text for `alt` attributes. - Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from this story. === END ARTIFACT ===
